title: Octagons and stars of the Shah-i-Zinda (Samarkand)
subtitle: Shah-i-Zinda, Samarkand

construction.note: The finished design was read from Brian Wichmann’s F254L drawing, its corners snapped to exact values. We devised the construction; the drawing gives no steps.
construction.changes: The compass steps, their order and the named points are ours. The comparison with the drawing checks the finished lines, not how the design was first laid out.

credits.creator: Brian Wichmann
credits.note: The design was read from his drawing; the construction is ours. He lists the same design at Nur al-Din’s mosque in Hama (1163), the Eşrefoğlu mosque in Beyşehir, Amir Shaykhu’s stone floor in Cairo and the shrine of Sheikh Safi in Ardabil.

credits.creator: David Wade
credits.note: The real panel, compared by eye with the wall: regular octagons touching at their corners.

given.A: A corner of that octagon, where it touches the next one.

steps.text: Draw a horizontal straight line through O and A. Draw a circle with centre O through A.
Draw a vertical line through O. The two lines cross the circle at A, B, C and D.
Draw the line through O that halves the angle AOB. Draw the line through O that halves the angle BOC. They cross the circle at E, F, G and H.
Join A, E, B, F, C, G, D and H with straight lines. This makes the octagon.

Draw a vertical line through A. Draw a vertical line through C. Draw a horizontal line through B. Draw a horizontal line through D. The four lines make a square with corners K1, K2, K3 and K4. Join them to mark the tile that repeats.

ink.text: Ink the octagon: from A through E, B and on round, back to A.

pattern.text: Put copies of the square tile side by side. The octagons touch at their corners, and a four-pointed star closes between every four of them.
